memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They devoted the city to the Lord and destroyed with the sword every living thing in it — men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep and donkeys. — Josh 6:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the hardest verses in the book, and we will not soften it into something comfortable. The judgment on Jericho was total and severe. We should feel the weight of it rather than explain it away. How do we understand such a passage as followers of a God of love?

First, we hold it firmly in its redemptive-historical setting. This was a unique moment of divine judgment on the Canaanite nations, whose wickedness had, in God's patient timing, reached its full measure (Gen 15:16). God had waited centuries. This was not random cruelty but the just judgment of a holy God against deeply entrenched evil, carried out through Israel as a one-time instrument. It is not a template for warfare or for how we treat others today.

Second, we let this passage teach us something we prefer to forget: that God is holy, that sin is deadly serious, and that judgment is real. Our age likes to imagine that sin has no consequences. Scripture will not let us think that. The severity here is meant to make us tremble at the reality of God's justice.

Third, and most importantly, we look to the cross. The same holy justice that fell on Jericho fell upon Jesus in our place. At Calvary, God poured out judgment on His own Son so that guilty people like us might be spared (Isa 53:5). We dare not read Jericho and feel superior; we should read it and flee to Christ, the only refuge from the judgment we all deserve.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you willing to take God's holiness and the reality of judgment seriously?
2. How does the cross help you make sense of a God who judges sin?
3. Does this hard passage drive you to gratitude that Christ bore judgment in your place?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, help me not to take sin lightly or imagine there are no consequences. Thank You that at the cross, Jesus bore the judgment I deserved. Draw me to Him as my only refuge. Amen.
